Forwarding e-mails

If you already have a incoming mail server for your domain, you may find the quickest way to get up and running is to simply forward e-mail from that server. You don't need to make any changes to your DNS to do this.

Just create an incoming route for the address you want to receive messages for and then you'll be provided with an e-mail address that messages can be forward to. Any message that is received to this address will be treated as if it had been sent directly to the address on the route.

The address to forward mail to can be found by clicking on the route and copying the field marked Address from the form.

Setting your MX records

If you don't already have a mail server on your domain, you can simply set your MX records to point to this system. Follow the instructions below to configure SPF & DKIM records for this domain. We highly recommend that you do this to ensure your messages are delivered correctly and quickly.

Check my records are correct Back to domain list

SPF Record

You need to add a TXT record at the apex/root of your domain (@) with the following content. If you already send mail from another service, you may just need to add include:spf.postal.example.com to your existing record. 

v=spf1 a mx include:spf.postal.example.com ~all

DKIM Record

You need to add a new TXT record with the name postal-PRTYAA._domainkey with the following content. 

v=DKIM1; t=s; h=sha256; p=MIGfMA0GCSqGSIb3DQEBAQUAA4GNADCBiQKBgQDWt+8XMJEoeOd5DW0ETcj7oklUiyd39h71ZsBxlZSOSydsb+ft26C/dfJmT/1W38oxhct1iuRN6ETNHNeLtwrysxhpmSiea/eU8Iv3s4WVgdTJyneTH++yuXwOyEmb1opc7igSRfbFLkeVcYm45rnzbjf/26UaFwmtZlxPI0LZrQIDAQAB;

Regenerate DKIM key

Return Path

This is optional but we recommend adding this to improve deliverability. You should add a CNAME record at psrp.mail.example.com to point to the hostname below. 

rp.postal.example.com

MX Records

If you wish to receive incoming e-mail for this domain, you need to add the following MX records to the domain. You don't have to do this and we'll only tell you if they're set up or not. Both records should be priority 10.

Filtering your messages

You can filter your messages on a number of attributes. At present, it is not possible to search the content of your messages. To filter though, you can insert any of the strings as shown opposite into the box above and press enter.

to: rachel@example.com
Returns all mail addressed to the address provided.
from: tom@example.com
Returns all mail sent from to the address provided.
status: pending
Returns all messages with the status provided. The suitable statuses are: pending, sent, held, softfail, hardfail and bounced.
before: yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm
Returns any message received before the given timestamp.
after: yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm
Returns any message received after the given timestamp.
msgid: 57f3a85b35545@server01.mail
Returns any message with the given Message-ID header.
tag: password-reset
Returns any message tagged with the tag provided.
spam: yes
By default, spam is not shown in results. To show spam instead of non-spam, just add this to the query.
order: oldest-first
By default, newest messages are shown first. To show oldest messages first, you can add this.

Filtering your messages

You can filter your messages on a number of attributes. At present, it is not possible to search the content of your messages. To filter though, you can insert any of the strings as shown opposite into the box above and press enter.

to: rachel@example.com
Returns all mail addressed to the address provided.
from: tom@example.com
Returns all mail sent from to the address provided.
status: pending
Returns all messages with the status provided. The suitable statuses are: pending, sent, held, softfail, hardfail and bounced.
before: yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm
Returns any message received before the given timestamp.
after: yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm
Returns any message received after the given timestamp.
msgid: 57f3a85b35545@server01.mail
Returns any message with the given Message-ID header.
tag: password-reset
Returns any message tagged with the tag provided.
spam: yes
By default, spam is not shown in results. To show spam instead of non-spam, just add this to the query.
order: oldest-first
By default, newest messages are shown first. To show oldest messages first, you can add this.
